episode_title: The 10 CMMC Questions Defense Suppliers Ask Us Most: A Self-Check for Your Compliance Program

real_qa.q: Do defense suppliers still need to worry about CMMC compliance in 2025 despite the Department of War certification pause?
real_qa.r: Yes, companies must still be NIST 800-171 and CMMC level two compliant even though certification on contracts is paused. The Department of War implemented a 60-day pause on requiring certifications, but compliance itself remains mandatory. C-through-PAOs are still conducting assessments, and certifications still provide value because a third party validating compliance lowers risk compared to self-attested claims.

real_qa.q: How do defense suppliers determine whether they must achieve CMMC level one or level two?
real_qa.r: The primary way is to check if your prime or the government told you to be at a specific level. Look for DFARS clauses 252.204-7012, 7019, or 7021 on your contracts. Level two applies if you handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Level one applies to Federal Contract Information (FCI), which is any non-public information about the contract. You should push back and ask your prime to clearly mark what data is CUI versus FCI so you know what you actually need to protect.
real_qa.requete: CMMC level one versus level two determination

real_qa.q: What is the most common documentation gap that causes CMMC assessment failures for defense contractors?
real_qa.r: The most critical gap is the lack of ongoing management and maintenance of security controls. Many companies implement technical controls like antivirus, endpoint protection, or backups, then fail to maintain them. For example, backup systems that have not been tested regularly or that throw errors are essentially not backups at all. CMMC and NIST 800-171 require continuous monitoring and care-and-feeding of the environment, not just initial setup.
real_qa.requete: CMMC assessment common failures documentation maintenance

real_qa.q: What is the Federal Contract Information (FCI) rule for CMMC level one compliance?
real_qa.r: Federal Contract Information is any information about a contract that is not public. A practical way to identify FCI is: if you have to log in to see the information, it is not available without logging in, then that information is probably FCI. Level one must be part of the contract, and your prime should specify 'for this contract, you have to be at level one.' Companies are increasingly receiving level one requirements.
real_qa.requete: Federal Contract Information FCI definition CMMC level one

real_qa.q: What date is the deadline for new CMMC rulemaking if the Department of War does not act?
real_qa.r: If the Department of War does not make any fresh rulemaking additions to Code of Federal Regulations by November 10, 2028, the previous CMMC requirements automatically switch back on. The pause is essentially open-ended, but there is this 2028 deadline that serves as a trigger for action.
